text.p: Federal investigators expanded a search of medical offices around El Paso, Texas and seized documents from doctors affiliated with local hospitals operated by Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, the New York Times said Friday.
The search was now said to be completed, according to the newspaper, which cited people familiar with the situation.

On Wednesday, Columbia/HCA said its El Paso, Texas operations were served with search warrants in connection with a federal investigation. The company said the warrants requested various records and documents.
It said then it had not been informed of the allegations but believed the investigation was limited to its El Paso facilities.

Sources close to the situation were quoted in the paper as saying the investigation also involved the Defense Department's Criminal Investigation Service, in addition to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Internal Revenue Service and the Department of Health and Human Services.
Investigators sought a range of documents, including financial, billing and medical records, the newspaper said.
